answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by linking power to long, verified history instead of upfront payment. A brand-new identity arrives at dawn with zero standing and must earn trust one epoch at a time, so mass-registering wallets yields nothing. Unlike money, a proven record cannot be split or lent; it grows only through real work, the way a garden produces fruit only after patient tending. Because influence also ebbs with the tide — old inactive accounts lose weight — a sybil farm that creates thousands of hollow identities can never harvest meaningful power from them.
